Abstract
People increasingly use language models to support life decisions. Many such
decisions involve a probabilistic forecast: How likely is a major life event, a natural
disaster, or an economic outcome? Users of language models may implicitly trust

from the sentiment in news text. However, backtesting such strategies poses a challenge
because LLMs are trained on many years of data, and backtesting produces biased results
if the training and backtesting periods overlap. This bias can take two forms: a look-ahead
